messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Confirming spend aperture & procurement trigger — Orchard AI

Samir — great to connect earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can align the pilot vs committed path: 

Call recap (pulled from our notes)
- Use case: live customer-facing summarization + search indexing for product docs
- Pilot expected Q2 (3–6 month pilot) with potential scale in Q3
- Estimated token profile: short chat + doc ingest mix; we discussed a range to capture uncertainty (monthly tokens)

Asks / next steps from Redwood
1) Can you confirm the monthly token range you want us to price for the pilot and 3–6 month steady state? We sketched: low=150M, mid=400M, high=900M tokens/month — please adjust.
2) Procurement trigger — what monthly spend or PO threshold routes this to procurement? (common examples: $25k/month, $50k/month, $100k/month).
3) Any compliance gating we should include in the pricing/OPS package (SOC 2, data residency, contract MSA redlines)?

High-level unit economics (examples only)
- Pilot (on-demand, no commit): ~$340–$420 per 1M tokens (depends on model family + latency SLO)
- Committed bands (3–12 month reserve): target $/1M tokens can fall to ~$180–$260 at larger committed volumes and with caching/quantization optimizations

Illustrative monthly spend examples (rounded)
- 150M tokens @ $340/1M ≈ $51k/month
- 400M tokens @ $260/1M (mid committed) ≈ $104k/month
- 900M tokens @ $200/1M (higher commit) ≈ $180k/month

I attached a quick cost estimate sheet and a simple mutual action plan template to make it easier for procurement to see the path. If you can confirm the token range and the procurement threshold we’ll produce a short pricing table and a suggested PO/commit cadence (monthly vs quarterly billing + recommended commit length) for finance to review.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the token-range confirmation and procurement contact.

Tessa Morgan

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@orchard.ai>

Date: Mon, 14 Mar 2027 17:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Confirming spend aperture & procurement trigger — Orchard AI

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Token range: the team’s comfortable with your low/mid/high framing. Our internal baseline today is ~120M tokens/month for the prototype. We expect production ramp to ~350–700M by end of Q3 depending on adoption. 

2) Budget / procurement trigger: finance flags any vendor spend > $75k/month for additional review. Anything above $200k/month needs VP-level signoff and an existing multi-month PO. We typically try to avoid >$200k/month without a committed contract.

3) Compliance: SOC 2 Type II is required, and we prefer vendor-hosted instances in us-west for now. We’ll need the vendor packet (W-9, insurance cert, SOC 2 report) for purchases > $25k.

Priya (cc’d) runs procurement — Priya, can you confirm typical timeline for a PO once vendor packet and MSA are in hand? Also looping in our engineering lead for technical gating.

—Samir
Head of Product, Orchard AI

Samir / Tessa — quick follow from our pricing desk after reviewing the ranges: 

- Pilot (no commit): we should price conservatively (example: $330–$400 / 1M). Pilot pricing keeps flexibility but unit costs are higher.
- Starter commit (3-month, reserve): 200–400M band — target $/1M = $240–$280. This is often the sweet spot where caching + prefix reuse matters most.
- Growth commit (6–12 month): 400–1,000M band — target $/1M = $165–$230 depending on model mix + quantization.

Recommendations for procurement path: 
1) If finance threshold is $75k/month as you noted, propose a 3-month committed band at ~300M tokens to keep month-to-month PO below the $75k trigger during the initial ramp. That gets Orchard closer to $/1M targets while avoiding heavy VP signoff.
2) If Orchard is willing to do a 6-month reserve we can lock a lower $/1M (we can granularize discounts into caching, reserved compute, and model-variant tiers).

I attached the estimate workbook (redwood_cost_estimate_v2.xlsx) with line-item scenarios (pilot vs 3mo commit vs 6mo commit). Also added a short sample PO wording and an MSA link.

Vivek — if you have any ops notes for data residency / SOC2 timelines please add.

Ben Carter

Hi all — thanks for the context. Procurement timeline and asks from Orchard: 

- Vendor packet required (W-9, cert of insurance, SOC 2 Type II) — once we receive full packet + MSA review, PO approval typically 10–14 business days for amounts <$100k/quarter. 
- For recurring spend > $100k/quarter (which maps to ~>$33k/month), we need a standard vendor onboarding and a 3rd party risk review; that can add ~7–10 business days. 
- If the expected monthly spend will hit $75k+ in the near term we will want a 3–6 month PO in place; finance will require the MSA and a pricing table showing committed unit economics.

Action items for Redwood: please send an itemized pricing table (pilot vs 3mo vs 6mo commit), the vendor packet (see list above), and a draft MSA. We’ll prioritize review once materials are complete.

Priya Malhotra
Procurement Lead, Orchard AI
